levies.label: Medicare levy on investment income
levies.plain_english: Australia adds a 2% Medicare levy on top of income tax. It applies to your dividends and net rent each year, just like salary.

meta.source_title: ATO — Medicare levy
meta.note: Low-income reduction and Medicare levy surcharge ignored.

levies.label: Medicare levy on the pre-July-2027 capital gain
levies.plain_english: The discounted capital gain is part of your taxable income in the year you sell, so the 2% Medicare levy applies to it. For the part of the gain made before 1 July 2027, half the gain is taxable.

meta.source_title: ATO — Medicare levy

levies.label: Medicare levy on the post-July-2027 capital gain
levies.plain_english: For the part of the gain made after 1 July 2027 the whole inflation-adjusted (real) gain is taxable income, so the 2% Medicare levy applies to all of it. The 30% minimum tax does not include the Medicare levy.

meta.source_title: Budget 2026–27 Tax Explainer — Negative gearing and CGT reform
meta.note: Gain is split at 1 July 2027 using the simulated value on that date (the ATO allows a valuation or an apportionment formula). Indexation uses the CPI input. Selling costs are not deducted from the gain. Recipients of income support are exempt from the minimum tax (not modelled).

ingress.label: Brokerage on purchase
ingress.plain_english: There is no stamp duty on ASX-listed shares or ETFs. A typical online broker charges about 0.1% to buy, which we treat as a cost rather than a tax.

meta.source_title: ASX — Fees and charges (brokerage is set by the broker; 0.1% assumed)

growth.label: Income tax on dividends (with franking credits)
growth.plain_english: Dividends are added to your other income and taxed at your marginal rate. Franked dividends come with a credit for the 30% company tax already paid, which is subtracted from your bill (and refunded if it exceeds it). Roughly 70% of ASX dividends are franked.

meta.source_title: ATO — Dividends and franking credits

egress.label: Capital gains tax on the pre-July-2027 gain (50% discount)
egress.plain_english: The part of your gain that built up before 1 July 2027 keeps the old rules: half of it is added to your income in the year you sell your shares or ETF units and taxed at your marginal rate. Index-fund units are CGT assets of the individual, so the reform applies when you sell them.

meta.source_title: ATO — CGT reform: 50% discount retained for gains accrued before 1 July 2027
meta.note: The gain up to 1 July 2027 is measured from the simulated value on that date.

egress.label: Capital gains tax on the post-July-2027 gain (indexed, 30% minimum)
egress.plain_english: From 1 July 2027 the 50% discount is replaced. The value on 1 July 2027 becomes your cost base, it is increased by inflation (CPI), and the whole remaining real gain is added to your income. If that works out below 30%, a minimum tax tops it up to 30% of the real gain. This was legislated after the 12 May 2026 Budget.

meta.source_title: Budget 2026–27 Tax Explainer — cost base indexation and 30% minimum tax
meta.note: Gain is split at 1 July 2027 using the simulated value on that date (the ATO allows a valuation or an apportionment formula). Indexation uses the CPI input. Selling costs are not deducted from the gain. Recipients of income support are exempt from the minimum tax (not modelled).

ingress.label: NSW transfer (stamp) duty

meta.source_title: Revenue NSW — Transfer duty rates (thresholds indexed annually)

ingress.plain_english: Buying a property in NSW triggers transfer duty, a one-off state tax charged on a sliding scale of the purchase price. On a AUD 1.5m purchase it is roughly 4.5%, paid up front before the asset earns anything.

meta.source_title: Revenue NSW — Transfer duty
meta.note: Surcharge purchaser duty for foreign buyers not modelled.

ingress.label: Conveyancing and registration
ingress.plain_english: Legal conveyancing and title registration fees on purchase, treated as a flat cost rather than a tax.

meta.source_title: NSW Government — Buying property (fees vary; AUD 3,000 assumed)

growth.label: Income tax on net rent
growth.plain_english: Rent, after deducting running costs such as management fees, insurance and repairs, is added to your other income and taxed at your marginal rate every year. Because this is an established property bought after 12 May 2026, from 1 July 2027 any rental loss could only offset residential property income, not your salary; this scenario has no loan, so it makes no loss.

meta.source_title: ATO — Residential rental properties
meta.note: Depreciation not modelled; costs fixed at assumptions.property.cost_rate of gross rent. Negative gearing restriction (2026–27 Budget) noted but has no effect without leverage.

growth.label: NSW land tax

meta.source_title: Revenue NSW — Land tax thresholds and rates (2025 tax year; thresholds frozen)

growth.plain_english: Investment property in NSW attracts annual land tax on the unimproved land value above a threshold (AUD 1.075m in 2025). The land is assumed to be 60% of the property's value. A AUD 100 base charge is ignored.

meta.source_title: Revenue NSW — Land tax
meta.note: Council rates excluded (treated as part of running costs).

egress.label: Capital gains tax on the pre-July-2027 gain (50% discount)
egress.plain_english: The part of your gain that built up before 1 July 2027 keeps the old rules: half of it is added to your income in the year you sell the property and taxed at your marginal rate. Stamp duty and purchase costs form part of the cost base.

meta.note: The gain up to 1 July 2027 is measured from the simulated value on that date.

The value on 1 July 2027 becomes your cost base, it is increased by inflation (CPI), and the whole remaining real gain is added to your income. If that works out below 30%, a minimum tax tops it up to 30% of the real gain. This was legislated after the 12 May 2026 Budget.

egress.label: Selling agent commission
egress.plain_english: Real-estate agents in Sydney typically charge around 2% of the sale price. It is a cost, not a tax, but it still reduces what you walk away with.
